verdict: Useful synthetic ranking and fresh-process timing evidence; insufficient to claim stale-content eviction or reproducible independently rebuilt semantic rankings.

findings.issue: Edit lifecycle checks only whether the same probe ID appears for the replacement query. An engine retaining both old and new representations passes. Inspect stored content/version or vectors; semantic candidate presence alone is insufficient.

stableAcrossPasses describes one index only. Identical recorded inputs and code produced zvec top1 14/20 and 13/20 across fresh builds; q001, q008, q017 and q023 changed ordering. Report cross-build variation separately.

Suite and harness are hashed at report end, allowing edits during execution to misattribute code. Snapshot before the run and detect subsequent changes; imported search code and model digests belong in computational provenance.

scope: Cold processes really reopen indexes. All three completed cold rankings match the corresponding warm rankings. They are three different queries once each, with warm filesystem/model caches, not cold-disk or repeated-identical-query variability.

Frozen union is correctly lexical-first five plus five, deduplicated. All 20 positive labels already occur in lexical top5; this suite cannot demonstrate additional union recall or better first-result ranks from that policy.
Inactive units are filtered before indexing. Deletion tests active-projection removal, not integrated Promptus lifecycle changes.
Normal-path output confinement resolves parent symlinks and uses exclusive writes. Fixture roots are process-created temp directories. Fetch overrides are not an OS network sandbox.
Only the retry supports four-engine comparison; the original receipt preserves QMD's IPC failure.
dispositionAtReview: Preserve the receipts. Strengthen stale-content and provenance checks before broader correctness claims. Record semantic ranking variability. No benchmark or source edit was performed by the auditor.
